Lee Seo-jin Jokes He’s Past His ‘Porter’ Days in Banter with Kim Yong-gun

The beloved Korean variety star reflects on aging out of his iconic travel-show role alongside veteran actor Kim Yong-gun.

BY HALLYUZINE SEOUL DESK • NOV 26, 2026
THE DOSSIER: KEY FACTS BRIEFING
  • Featured Figures: Variety icon Lee Seo-jin and veteran actor Kim Yong-gun
  • Cultural Context: References Lee Seo-jin's legendary 'porter' persona from classic Korean travel-reality television
  • Global Appeal: Highlights the enduring charm of intergenerational chemistry in K-variety programming

A Playful Passing of the Torch

Few figures in Korean entertainment have mastered the art of reluctant charm quite like Lee Seo-jin. Known globally for his deadpan humor and effortless leadership in hit reality series, the actor recently sparked laughter among fans by declaring that he is officially past the age of playing the dutiful 'porter' for his senior colleagues. The remark came during a candid exchange with veteran actor Kim Yong-gun, who playfully countered by noting that Lee has been linking arms with him quite often lately—a subtle, affectionate nod to their deepening camaraderie.

For international K-culture enthusiasts, the banter immediately evokes nostalgia for the golden era of Korean travel-reality television. Lee Seo-jin first cemented his status as the nation’s favorite grumbling caretaker in Grandpas Over Flowers, where he was famously tasked with carrying luggage, navigating foreign transit systems, and managing budgets for a cast of legendary senior actors. His willingness to complain openly while quietly taking care of every detail became a blueprint for modern K-variety storytelling.

The Evolution of K-Variety’s Reluctant Hero

Over the past decade, Lee Seo-jin has transitioned from a dramatic leading man into one of South Korea’s most bankable unscripted personalities. Whether running pop-up restaurants abroad in Youn’s Kitchen and Jinny’s Kitchen or guiding senior stars across Europe, his appeal lies in his authenticity. Unlike traditional variety hosts who rely on exaggerated slapstick, Lee brings a dry, grounded wit that resonates strongly with global audiences accustomed to understated comedy.

His latest exchange with Kim Yong-gun underscores how these unscripted relationships continue to evolve off-screen and on-camera. As Lee steps into a more seasoned phase of his career, the dynamic shifts from a dutiful younger assistant to an equal, affectionate companion. Kim’s teasing observation about Lee linking arms highlights the genuine warmth that underpins their public persona—a quality that keeps international viewers tuning in.

Why Intergenerational Chemistry Still Rules

In an era dominated by fast-paced idol content and high-stakes survival shows, the enduring popularity of Lee Seo-jin and Kim Yong-gun’s rapport speaks to a core pillar of Korean entertainment: respect blended with playful familiarity. Global fans have increasingly gravitated toward Korean reality formats precisely because they showcase authentic, cross-generational bonds that feel both culturally specific and universally relatable.

Even if Lee Seo-jin insists his heavy-lifting days are behind him, his presence in K-variety remains indispensable. As Korean unscripted television continues to expand its footprint on global streaming platforms, moments of genuine, unforced humor between veteran stars remind audiences why the genre’s human touch remains its greatest export.
